content.title: How to watch Caitlin Clark and Team USA at FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup 2026 Qualifiers
content.text: The United States women’s basketball team will continue their FIBA Women’s World Cup 2026 preparations when they compete in the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup 2026 Qualifiers in San Juan, Puerto Rico, from 11-17 March. Four qualifying tournaments will take place around the world during that period, with 24 teams bidding for the remaining 11 spots at the showpiece taking place from 4-13 September in Germany. The U.S. secured its place at the World Cup after sweeping the FIBA Women’s Americas Cup in 2025, joining hosts Germany and other already-qualified continental champions, Nigeria, Australia and Belgium. That means their five-game tournament in San Juan will be more about stress-testing and future-planning than results, while the five other teams compete for their spots in Berlin. How the reigning world champions go under new head coach Kara Lawson will be a great point of intrigue. The roster assembled to take on Puerto Rico, Senegal, Italy, New Zealand and Spain is made up of a blend of veteran stars, such as Olympic champions Kahleah Copper, Chelsea Gray and Kelsey Plum, and players that have risen through the U.S. junior ranks, including the past two WNBA rookies of the year, Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers. Clark’s potential debut for the senior U.S. team will likely be studied closely, given that the Indiana Fever star played in just 13 games last WNBA season due to injury, and hasn't been competitively on court since she was ruled out with injury. On the subject of her absence, the 24-year-old spoke about finding herself again at the recent training camp in December, and that she is likely to be a little bit rusty if, and when, she does hit the hardwood. The FIBA stage, however, is one Clark knows well, having twice competed at the U19 Women’s Basketball World Cup. In her second appearance in Debrecen, Hungary, she was named MVP, underlining her future international potential.
